case_title: Shajahan v. State rep. by Inspector of Police
statutory_provisions: IPC s.457, s.395, s.396, s.302 r/w s.34 (s.396 r/w s.34 on which conviction rests)
weapon: Jute rope (used for strangulation); accused not armed per court
evidence_type: Recovery of jewels; identification of jewels by pawn shop owner and pledgers; pawn registers (documentary); police and witness testimony; hostile witnesses
confession: Yes: confession statements of accused (Raja Mohammad, Basheer, Shajahan, Babu) led to recoveries; the court relied on the recoveries and identification of jewels
aggravating_circumstances: Murder by strangulation during dacoity; jewellery worth about Rs.12,00,000 robbed
mitigating_circumstances: Accused were not armed; long lapse of time since the 2002 occurrence; accused in custody for over ten years
trial_court_outcome: All five convicted under s.396 r/w s.34 IPC; ten years rigorous imprisonment; no separate s.302 conviction
high_court_outcome: State's appeal allowed: s.396 sentence enhanced to life imprisonment; appeals of Shajahan and Raja Mohammad dismissed; s.302 not considered
offence_finally_established: IPC s.396 r/w s.34 (dacoity with murder)
neutral_facts: On the intervening night of 13/14 November 2002, at about 1.30 a.m., several men allegedly planned to rob a pawn broking shop whose owner is named as the complainant. One accused allegedly held the legs of the victim, who was sleeping inside the shop, while another allegedly sat on his chest, tied a jute rope around his neck and strangled him to death. The others allegedly robbed jewellery of about 4.788 kg of gold and 5.595 kg of silver, valued at about Rs.12,00,000. The shop sweeper found the victim dead on the morning of 13 November 2002 and informed the owner, who lodged a complaint with the police. During the investigation, one accused was arrested and, on his confession, a sum of money and jewellery were recovered; further confessions led to recoveries of jewellery from several locations, including a jewellery shop and houses. On 6 February 2003, at about 1.30 a.m., two accused on a two-wheeler were intercepted by police; they ran but were caught, and jewels were recovered from a cover on the petrol tank. The shop owner and several persons who had pledged jewels identified the recovered items, and the shop's registers recorded the pledges. Two witnesses to the arrests turned hostile on identifying the accused, but the investigating officer gave evidence of the arrests and recoveries.
offence_severity: Death or imprisonment for life (as stated in the judgment); minimum not stated
physical_harm: Death of Muthukrishnan by strangulation with a jute rope
financial_property_loss: Gold 4.788 kg and silver 5.595 kg, worth about Rs.12,00,000
premeditation_planning: Not identified by the court; prosecution alleged a common intention to commit robbery
motive: alleged: robbery of jewellery from the pawn shop
key_evidence_accepted: Evidence of PW-15 and PW-17; recovery of jewels identified by PW-1 and PWs 7 to 14; pawn registers corroborating pledges; evidence of IO PW-37 on arrests and recovery of jewels from the two-wheeler
witness_credibility: PWs 21 and 22 turned hostile on identification but their evidence on the two-wheeler and recovery was read with PW-37; hostility did not affect the case. PW-1's evidence corroborated by registers
post_offence_conduct: Accused Basheer and Shajahan ran when intercepted by police and were caught
custody_duration: More than ten years, as stated in the judgment
trial_duration: offence: 13/14.11.2002; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 03.09.2010; Supreme Court: 16.02.2018
legal_representation: Accused/appellants: Amit Kumar, R. Balasubramanian, B. Karunakaran, S. Gowthaman, K. G. Krishnaraj, S. Shanthakumari. State: M. Yogesh Kanna, Mrs. Sujatha Bagadhi
investigation_status: FIR/complaint registered (Crime No.257 of 2002); investigation completed; chargesheet filed; 37 prosecution witnesses examined at trial
appeal_history: Trial court: s.396 r/w s.34, ten years RI for all five. High Court: State appeal allowed, sentence enhanced to life; accused's appeals dismissed. Supreme Court: conviction maintained, sentence reduced to ten years for Basheer, Shajahan and Babu; Raja Mohammad's conviction maintained
legal_principle_applied: Companions in a dacoity are liable under s.396 for murder by a co-dacoit even without direct participation; sentencing discretion lies between death/life and lesser punishment under s.396
precedent_relied_upon: Dinesh alias Buddha v. State of Rajasthan (2006) 3 SCC 771 (relied on by the High Court; referred to by the Supreme Court)
sentencing_rationale: Long lapse of time since the 2002 occurrence, facts and circumstances, and accused not being armed; sentence reduced to ten years as per trial court
judicial_mitigating_factors: Accused not armed; long lapse of time since 2002 occurrence
judicial_aggravating_factors: Offence under s.396 viewed with seriousness; murder committed in course of dacoity
other_sentence_order: Release forthwith of appellants (Basheer, Shajahan, Babu) if not required in any other case
